A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaGen framework. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout, including v2's Appendices A-J. The supplied v1 ends with references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original nuScenes generation, forecasting, module-ablation and interactive-editing results in Tables 1-5 and Figures 6-7.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices H-J report original generation, detection, temporal-consistency, forecasting, ablation and robustness results, including additional KITTI-360 experiments.

M1.justification: The LDM, SDE, NM and autoregressive loop remain. Equation (6) changes the specified attention query from bounding-box features to intermediate U-Net features, and Section 4.4 introduces a box-free forecasting variant. Expanded encoder and convolution descriptions primarily disclose implementation details.

E1.justification: The nuScenes-only evaluation expands to KITTI-360, introducing 64-beam scans alongside nuScenes' 32-beam scans. v2 also evaluates downstream 3D object detection and generation under perturbed or missing bounding-box conditions, substantially broadening task and input-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds UniScene, OpenDWM, DriveLiDAR4D and LiDARCrafter to the nuScenes generation comparison, retaining LiDARGen, LiDM and RangeLDM. Temporal comparisons additionally include OpenDWM-DiT. The existing 4D-Occ and ViDAR forecasting comparators remain.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce TTCE/CTC, KITTI-360 FRD/FPD, detection mAP/NDS and object-level CD/EMD. Additional protocols sweep 10-200 denoising steps and specify bounding-box perturbation and dropping probabilities. Newly disclosed training settings do not establish that existing experiments changed their training budgets.

E4.justification: v2 extends the SDE/NM ablations with temporal-consistency measurements and revised horizon selections. It adds a box-free control, denoising-step accuracy/latency analysis, and systematic bounding-box shifting/dropping tests in Tables 6-9 and Appendix H. The original interactive-editing demonstration is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The additional experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Numerous results are added, and LaGen's reported nuScenes MMD/JSD changes from 0.35/3.97 in v1 Table 2 to 0.11/2.77 in v2 Table 1 under unchanged table scaling. Protocol continuity is insufficient to establish a controlled performance gain. New Table 5 favors LaGen on CTC but LiDARCrafter on TTCE. Some duplicated results conflict: two-frame 4D-Occ's 9.5-second CD is 55.47 in v2 main Table 6 and 65.92 in supplementary Table 5.

T1.justification: New Appendices E-F introduce an autoregressive error recursion, Taylor-expansion/Jacobian-regularization argument, claimed contraction guarantee, and motion assumptions supporting SDE. v1 contains algorithm equations and intuitive motivation but lacks these theoretical derivations. The contraction guarantee is asserted without establishing the required spectral-radius bound.

C1.justification: The central claim of interactive, single-frame-initialized autoregressive LiDAR generation and the SDE/NM contributions remain. v2 drops the nuScenes evaluation protocol as a headline contribution and explicitly promotes the conditional feature encoder in the contribution list.

C2.justification: v2 explains current bounding boxes as simulator feedback and interprets the benefit of updated scene information over historical-input forecasting. It adds sensor-type and crowded-scene matching limitations, background-transformation reasoning, and an accuracy/latency tradeoff discussion. Its positive SDE interpretation also replaces v1's warning about additional errors at very long horizons.

D1.justification: v2 adds training epochs/steps, batch size, learning rate, scheduler, GPU hardware/time, pretrained VAE initialization, circular convolutions, sampling settings, metric preprocessing, SDE pseudocode and a code-access URL. These substantially expand reproducibility information. However, v1's explicit construction of 176 valid sequences containing 20 frames is omitted.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to contemporary generators including Genesis, DriveLiDAR4D, UniScene, OpenDWM, LiDARCrafter and La La LiDAR. v2 acknowledges LiDARCrafter's autoregressive generation and distinguishes LaGen through interactive per-step control, materially refining its novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the experimental narrative into generation, temporal consistency and downstream forecasting, replacing the dedicated benchmark subsection. It consolidates the standalone inference subsection, revises introductory positioning and contribution wording, and adds extensive organized technical explanations throughout the supplement.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with retained figures resized and repositioned and several captions shortened. Forecasting tables are consolidated, generation comparisons gain conditional/unconditional grouping, and new tables, SDE visualizations, metric curves and full-sequence comparison grids substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical support through relevant conditional-generation comparators, a box-free forecasting control, temporal-consistency measurements, and robustness/latency evaluations. Detailed implementation disclosures and explicit applicability limits also materially strengthen reproducibility and interpretation. These gains outweigh reporting regressions: the benchmark-construction recipe disappears, duplicated baseline scores conflict, and Appendix E does not establish its claimed contraction guarantee. The improvement rests on stronger evaluation and documentation, not simply additional pages or better reported scores.
